title: Observability: tag runtime metrics with profile_id/sku/scheduling_mode + export new counters/histograms
creator: Allison Grant
description:
Context
- As we roll out the hardware tuning profiles pack (H100/L40S/B200), SRE/Infra need the ability to attribute changes in latency, throughput, and error rates to the active profile, detected hardware SKU, and scheduling mode.
- Today, most runtime latency histograms/counters are tagged by route/model/region, but not by “profile identity”. This makes canary analysis and rollback decisions slower and less deterministic.

Goal
1) Add low-cardinality runtime metric tags:
   - profile_id (e.g., "h100-default", "l40s-stable", "b200-preview")
   - profile_version (e.g., "1.0.0")
   - sku (e.g., "H100-SXM", "H100-PCIe", "L40S", "B200")
   - scheduling_mode (e.g., "mixed_bucket_v1", "fifo", "prefill_priority")
2) Export/standardize additional counters + histograms required for validating expected behavior:
   - queueing vs compute split (scheduler_queue_ms + compute stage histograms)
   - profile selection outcomes (compatibility gate failures, fallback reasons)
   - profile mismatch / drift detection signals (e.g., model reload across pools)

Non-goals
- Adding high-cardinality tags (customer_id, request_id, full model revision hash) to global metrics.
- Building dashboards here (tracked in dashboard spec + observability-pack PR). This ticket is runtime instrumentation only.

Implementation notes
Tagging strategy (cardinality constraints)
- All new tags MUST be drawn from bounded sets:
  - sku: <= ~10 values across fleet
  - scheduling_mode: <= ~5 values per runtime major
  - profile_id/profile_version: bounded by the shipped profile pack (expected < 50 total active combinations)
- Do NOT add model_id or route to the same metric series if it already has high fanout. Prefer two parallel metrics when needed:
  - Global SLO series: tagged with sku/profile_id/scheduling_mode (no model/route)
  - Debug series: tagged with model_family or route_bucket only (no profile_id) when necessary
- Ensure tags are attached at the “request context” boundary so they apply consistently across:
  - request latency histograms
  - stage spans (prefill/decode)
  - scheduler enqueue/dequeue
  - admission control drops

Metric names and definitions (proposed)
(Note: names should match existing Redwood conventions; final names can be adjusted during review, but the semantics must remain.)
1) Histograms
- runtime_request_latency_ms{sku,profile_id,profile_version,scheduling_mode,deploy_mode}
  - End-to-end per request, including queueing.
- runtime_scheduler_queue_ms{sku,profile_id,profile_version,scheduling_mode}
  - Time spent waiting in scheduler queue.
- runtime_prefill_compute_ms{sku,profile_id,profile_version}
  - Prefill compute time excluding queueing.
- runtime_decode_compute_ms{sku,profile_id,profile_version}
  - Decode compute time excluding queueing.
- runtime_admission_control_wait_ms{sku,profile_id,profile_version}
  - If present in codepath; otherwise omit.

2) Counters
- runtime_profile_selection_total{sku,selected_profile_id,reason}
  - reason examples: "exact_match", "compat_fallback", "default", "override_pin".
- runtime_profile_compat_reject_total{sku,profile_id,reason}
  - reason examples: "driver_too_old", "cuda_mismatch", "mig_unsupported", "insufficient_vram_headroom".
- runtime_profile_override_reject_total{sku,reason}
  - reason examples: "guardrail_headroom", "unknown_profile_version", "policy_disallowed".
- runtime_request_dropped_total{sku,profile_id,profile_version,drop_reason}
  - drop_reason examples: "queue_limit", "oom_prevented", "timeout".

3) Gauges (only if already supported in runtime metrics backend)
- runtime_active_profile_info{sku,profile_id,profile_version}
  - Emit as an info-style gauge (value=1). If gauge support is limited, prefer a periodic log line + rely on /health debug endpoint (separate ticket/PR).

Telemetry plumbing
- Wire tags through the existing metrics context object used by:
  - HTTP/gRPC request layer
  - scheduler
  - model execution pipeline
- For tracing:
  - Add span attributes (same keys) on top-level request span only.
  - Avoid duplicating on every child span to reduce payload size.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] For Hosted/Dedicated/Private, top-level latency histograms include sku + profile_id + profile_version + scheduling_mode tags.
- [ ] scheduler_queue_ms is exported and makes it possible to separate queueing regression from kernel/compute regression.
- [ ] profile selection and compatibility failures are counted with actionable reasons.
- [ ] Tag cardinality review: production canary shows no explosion in unique time series (SRE sign-off).
- [ ] Unit/integration tests cover:
  - default profile selection
  - override pinning path
  - compatibility gate refusal
  - tags present on emitted metrics
- [ ] Release note snippet provided to Connor O’Brien for runtime-1.22 checklist.

Rollout plan
- Land behind runtime-1.22 feature set; metrics should be additive (no breaking renames unless coordinated).
- Enable in Hosted canary cohort first; compare unique series + ingestion volume vs baseline.
- If ingestion spikes, disable debug series first (keep SLO series), then revert instrumentation if needed.

Links / related
- GitHub (runtime): PR-24935 (tag latency histograms with profile_id + sku; add scheduler_queue_ms)
- GitHub (runtime): PR-25063 (separate queueing vs compute time in traces; validate against expected behavior)
- GitHub (observability-pack): PR-221 (dashboards consuming these tags)
- Linear:
  - ENG-4930 Perf canary gating (consumes profile tags)
  - ENG-4923 Runtime selection logic (produces profile_id/profile_version)
  - ENG-4924 Scheduler tuning (defines scheduling_mode values)

Open questions
- Final tag key naming: "sku" vs "gpu_sku"; "scheduling_mode" vs "scheduler_mode". Prefer alignment with dashboard spec and existing naming.
- deploy_mode tag: if we already have an environment label that captures Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, re-use it; do not create redundant tags.
comments: 2026-01-16 (Caleb Johnson): Drafted metric/tag list. Biggest risk is accidental fanout when combined with route/model tags. Plan is to tag only the global SLO histograms and keep per-route series unchanged.

2026-01-24 (Sean Gallagher): SRE request: must include a queueing signal (scheduler_queue_ms) and a clear counter for compatibility gate failures with reason labels so on-call can identify driver/CUDA drift quickly.
2026-01-28 (Julian Moore): Scheduling_mode values agreed for v1: fifo, mixed_bucket_v1. We should emit the attribute at scheduler enqueue time to avoid missing tags on dropped requests.
2026-02-02 (Allison Grant): Please ensure profile_id/profile_version are applied consistently across latency and error counters; dashboards need to correlate p95 shifts with profile adoption panels.

2026-02-05 (Caleb Johnson): Opened PR-24935. Added scheduler_queue_ms and tagged request latency histogram with sku/profile_id/profile_version/scheduling_mode. Added safeguards to avoid tagging per-route histograms with profile_id (kept existing labels).

2026-02-10 (Rafael Mendes): Canary checklist update: add a step to verify time series count in metrics backend after enabling canary. Also want a quick way to query “compat rejects by reason” during B200 bring-up.

2026-02-18 (Caleb Johnson): Merged PR-25063 follow-up to separate queueing vs compute in traces. Confirmed tags appear on top-level span only. Canary showed stable series count (+~3% overall) and no ingestion alerts.
2026-02-20 (Allison Grant): Marking done. Dashboard work is tracked separately; runtime instrumentation is in runtime-1.22 branch.
